handoff: review#1: AC1-AC4 proven by tests; blocking F1: a local non-holder's update-branch gets a schema usage error (naming removed 'norn update') instead of its refusal, since boundary targets skip check for every verb; minors F2-F5, F8 (confirm D17 empty commits), nits F6-F7

findings.title: A local non-holder's non-mailbox verb gets a schema usage error instead of its refusal
findings.detail:
remoteTarget returns a `boundary` target under `local` for every caller of resolveTarget (line 169), not only for mailbox verbs; runHumanVerb then skips `opts.check` and `opts.noop` for it (lines 239-240) and calls `build`, and humanReceipt omits `attempt` for every kind (line 221), although only answer/approve/reject/unstick may lack it. Repro (two clones of one bare remote, record.policy local, gh-30 held by A at its ready gate): on B `norn story update-branch gh-30 --json` prints {"error":"invalid update: / must have required property 'attempt'; ...","do_instead":"norn update --help","code":"usage"} (exit 2), where before this slice it was refused (unknown_unit; with the check run, story_not_local / T7). The do_instead names a removed command (the harness's B7 guard throws on it). P8: a refusal must be a CliError with the rule's code. `story edit --auto` and `run cancel` survive only because they refuse on the claim before resolving.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Give remoteTarget the boundary cursor only when the verb goes through the mailbox (runHumanVerb's `opts.mailbox` path), or keep running `check` for boundary targets of non-mailbox kinds; in humanReceipt omit attempt only for the mailbox kinds. Add the update-branch (and run rerun) from a local non-holder case to mailbox-across-machines.test.ts.

findings.title: run rerun from a local non-holder posts an unvalidated unstick
findings.detail:
With `check` skipped, `norn run rerun gh-30 --step nosuch` on B (local) posts {kind: unstick, step: ready, to: nosuch} to the mailbox and exits 0 (reproduced); an unknown --step or --reset counter is no longer refused at the sender. D17 lists unstick among the mailbox kinds, so the holder judging it is in line with the spec, but neither AC nor test covers what the holder does with it.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Keep the sender-side checks that need no cursor (flags against the branch's workflow) or add a test that the holder rejects such a receipt into a Check item.

findings.title: rejected.json is never pruned, though its doc says tidy ages it out
findings.detail:
The schema comment says 'nothing deletes an entry but `norn tidy`'s age', but no tidy code reads or prunes rejectedReceiptsPath (only local.ts, local-facts.ts, paths.ts use it). Entries are filtered at read (openRejections, storyFinished) and the file grows forever on a busy holder.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Prune entries of finished or cleared stories (in tidy or when adding), or correct the comment.

findings.title: The rejected receipt is kept only after the mailbox ref is deleted
findings.detail:
rejectReceipt deletes the ref, traces, then keepRejected writes rejected.json. A crash between the delete and the write loses the Check item for good (the ref is gone), which is exactly the 'stale answer vanishes silently' B21 forbids. P6 spirit: record before the effect.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Call keepRejected (and the trace) before deleteMailbox; addRejectedReceipt already dedups by receipt_id, so a retry is harmless.

findings.title: Empty boundary commits are made for slices too, which no reader needs
findings.detail:
D17 makes a boundary commit even when nothing changed so a non-holder can read the story's last boundary. That is required for the story unit (check and gate steps never change a file, so without it the non-holder stamps a step the holder already left) and restores the cadence main had before gh-195 (norn-only commits are already tolerated by onlyNornCommitsSince). But lastBoundary (store/elsewhere.ts:681-689) skips every commit with Norn-Slice, and slices under local are refused as unknown units, so empty slice boundary commits only add history and a push (a CI run on the PR) per slice step. Also act decides this by sniffing the trailer name; decide could set it on BoundaryCommit.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: allowEmpty only when the trailers have Norn-Outcome and no Norn-Slice (or a BoundaryCommit flag set by decide for the story unit).

findings.title: boundaryCursor fakes a UnitState with a double cast
findings.detail:
`{ step, run: null, park: null } as unknown as UnitState` hands every check/build/before callback a state whose attempt, status, workflow_hash and round are undefined behind a type that says they exist; F1 is what that hides.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Give the boundary path its own narrow type (step only) so the compiler shows which callbacks read more.

findings.title: noteInHandoff's premise no longer holds
findings.detail:
Slice 07 added noteInHandoff so 'norn's next boundary commit has something of its own to carry'; with allowEmpty every step-ending commit is made anyway. The tests still pass and still mean what they say (BS5.2 owed commit held; C5 $done commit after approval), but the comments state a reason that is gone.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Update the comments (or drop the helper where the commit is a boundary) in a later touch.

findings.title: D17's 'made even when nothing else changed' goes beyond the person's answer
findings.detail:
The person's answer (receipt 0003, commit ad4be1a18) decided Norn-Next and step-only receipts; it did not mention empty commits. The implementer added the clause to D17 when the restored human block showed it was needed. The reasoning holds (see F5), but it reverses slice 07's 'no per-boundary norn commit' outcome and a person should confirm it at the gate.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Confirm at the slice/story gate; no code change needed if confirmed.
